title: Localization Delocalization Transition in Diffusion with Adaptive Resetting
abstract: Stochastic resetting can localize diffusion and generate nonequilibrium steady states, but the conditions under which spatially dependent resetting produces localization remain unclear. Here, we establish a general classification for diffusion under adaptive resetting, where the resetting rate $r(x)$ depends on position. For rates with the asymptotic scaling $r(x)\sim |x|^λ$, we identify a sharp threshold at $λ=-2$. For $λ>-2$, the steady state is localized and exhibits stretched-exponential tails, whereas for $λ<-2$, resetting is asymptotically too weak to localize the particle. Precisely at the marginal scaling $r(x)\sim |x|^{-2}$, a qualitatively new regime emerges: the steady state develops power-law tails with a temperature-dependent exponent and exhibits a finite-temperature delocalization transition. Thus, inverse-square resetting plays the role of the logarithmic potential in equilibrium, establishing a nonequilibrium counterpart of the temperature-driven delocalization seen there.
summary: This theoretical paper classifies diffusion under spatially dependent stochastic resetting by analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady state (NESS). It establishes a critical scaling exponent $\lambda = -2$, which separates localized diffusion (stretched-exponential tails) from a new, power-law decaying regime. This marginal case provides a nonequilibrium analogue to temperature-driven delocalization seen in equilibrium statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a general classification for diffusion under adaptive resetting, determining the nature of the non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) based on the spatial dependence of the resetting rate $r(x)$.
main_result: A sharp threshold exists at $r(x) \sim |x|^{-2}$; for stronger resetting ($\lambda > -2$), the state is localized with stretched-exponential tails, while the marginal case ($\lambda = -2$) yields a power-law tail, establishing a nonequilibrium counterpart to equilibrium delocalization.
method: The analysis involves solving the governing ordinary differential equation for the NESS using analytical ansatz solutions (stretched-exponential and power-law forms) and comparing these results to numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The model describes a particle undergoing diffusion (with coefficient $D$) subjected to an adaptive resetting rate $r(x)$ that scales as a power law, $r(x) \sim |x|^\lambda$. The system is analyzed by examining the steady-state probability distribution $p(x)$.
key_observables: The asymptotic decay exponent ($\eta$ or $\alpha$) of the NESS tails, and the critical temperature ($T_c$) marking the delocalization transition.
important_parameters: The exponent $\lambda$ characterizing the resetting rate $r(x) \sim |x|^\lambda$, and the ratio $r_0/D$ which determines the transition point.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the resetting rate $r(x)$ follows a power-law asymptotic form, $r(x) \simeq r_0|x|^\lambda$ for large $|x|$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the NESS under different $\lambda$ values, showing stretched-exponential decay for $\lambda > 0$ and illustrating the theoretical fit to the derived asymptotics.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the governing ODE for the NESS under adaptive resetting, deriving explicit forms for the steady-state tails in the localized ($\lambda > -2$) and marginal ($\lambda = -2$) regimes, drawing parallels to equilibrium potential theory.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous, non-equilibrium framework for understanding localization transitions, drawing direct analogies between quantum/classical confinement potentials and stochastic resetting mechanisms, which is relevant for open quantum systems dynamics.
